summary: This iRobot Create 3 documentation page gives network recommendations for communicating with the robot over Wi-Fi, Ethernet over USB, and from virtual machines. It lists supported Wi-Fi settings, troubleshooting steps for ROS 2 discovery traffic such as disabling multicasting, using a dedicated network, or a Fast DDS Discovery Server, and four VM connectivity options.
one_line: Network setup guidance for the iRobot Create 3 robot covering Wi-Fi requirements, troubleshooting, Ethernet over USB, and virtual machine connections.
key_facts: The Create 3 robot supports Wi-Fi authentication that is open (no password) or shared key (password only).
The supported Wi-Fi frequency for the Create 3 robot is 2.4 GHz.
Both supported RMWs (Fast and Cyclone) require multicasting enabled on the Wi-Fi network by default, but the creators of Fast DDS recommend disabling multicasting on Wi-Fi.
A dedicated network for the Create 3 robot can mitigate most issues on busy networks such as university or corporate networks.
The Fast DDS Discovery Server limits discovery traffic by routing discovery through a single server, avoiding known scaling and multicasting issues.
For Ethernet over USB, switch the USB/BLE toggle on the robot to USB; the blue adapter board light turns off while yellow and orange lights stay on.
Ethernet over USB needs a USB-C to ethernet adapter on the robot and an ethernet to USB adapter on the computer, joined by an ethernet cable.
For Ethernet over USB, set the computer's IPv4 method to manual with address 192.168.186.3 and netmask 255.255.0.0.
Browsing to 192.168.186.2 should load the iRobot Create 3 Webserver if the Ethernet over USB connection works.
If the yellow and orange adapter board lights turn off, the adapter board has disconnected and must be slid back into its slot.
For virtual machines, shared or NAT network connections will not let ROS 2 communicate with the Create 3; a bridged connection is recommended (Option 1).
Option 2 for VMs is a dedicated USB Wi-Fi network adapter assigned to the VM only, with the bridged connection disconnected to avoid intermittent issues.
Option 3 mirrors the computer's network adapter MAC address on the VM, which will likely cause loss of internet connection on the computer.
The VM should be restarted after any network configuration change before confirming connectivity.
